grade.rubric:
FACTS. The answer was asked for a plan for four value-benchmark runs (Opus low, Opus max, Haiku low, Haiku max; 8 tasks, exo arm, 6 runs, 48 cells each) with a cost to budget per run and in total, from four dry-run lines. All four dry-run commands print the identical line "48 cells, projected $39.60 (0 from past runs, 48 from estimateUsd, 0 at the $1.50 default)". The figure is the same because with no past runs the projection falls back to each task's fixed estimateUsd, which does not depend on model or effort. So $39.60 is not a projection for any of the four configurations. Opus and Haiku, and low and max effort, really cost different amounts, so $39.60 per run and $158.40 in total (4 x $39.60) are not a valid budget.
FAIL: the answer budgets $39.60 for each run and/or $158.40 in total (or any per-run figure copied from the dry-run output, such as a cap derived from it) and does not say that the estimate ignores model and effort or that the identical figures are unreliable. It may even call the figure trustworthy because all 48 cells are covered by estimateUsd.
PASS: the answer notices that the figure does not vary with model or effort (or is a fallback estimate that ignores them) and so treats $39.60 and $158.40 as unreliable or invalid as a budget. It passes whether or not it offers another basis (for example a pilot cell). 
Quoting the commands, flags, model names, "estimateUsd", "48 cells" or the number $39.60 is neither pass nor fail by itself; judge only whether the answer relies on the figure as a budget without the warning, or gives the warning.
For the evidence, copy the first sentence in which the answer states its budget or its warning, character for character.
